2027-04-07.title: Wednesday after New Sunday · He is our peace
readings: He is our peace; he has broken down the dividing wall
The lamp on the lampstand; pay attention to how you listen
2027-04-07.alt: Season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection), the week after New Sunday.
2027-04-07.verse: For he is our peace; in his flesh he has made both groups into one and has broken down the dividing wall, that is, the hostility between us.
theo: Christ is risen! On Easter evening the risen Lord stood among his frightened disciples and said, “Peace be with you.” Today St Paul explains how deep that peace goes. He writes to Christians who were not born Jews: “Remember that you were at that time without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers to the covenants of promise, having no hope and without God in the world. But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ.” Notice what Paul honors here: the commonwealth of Israel and the covenants of promise are a treasure. Gentile believers, which is to say almost all of us, have been brought near to Israel's hope, grafted, as Paul says elsewhere, onto the olive tree whose root supports us (Romans 11:17–18). The Church remembers with gratitude her spiritual bond with the Jewish people (Nostra Aetate 4). Then the great sentence: “For he is our peace; in his flesh he has made both groups into one and has broken down the dividing wall, that is, the hostility between us.” When Paul says that Christ “abolished the law with its commandments and ordinances,” he is speaking of the rules that kept Jew and Gentile apart as a wall; he does not mean that God's commandments no longer matter. Christ fulfills the Law, and in him both have “access in one Spirit to the Father.” Here is the whole Trinity in a single line, and the Cross is the place where hostility was put to death.

What walls still stand among us? Families divided over property, neighbors who have not spoken for years, the old wounds of caste that still mark some Christian communities in Kerala, suspicion between Churches that share one Baptism. Christ has already broken the wall in his flesh; our part is to stop rebuilding it. Our own Church knows something of this grace: in 1930 Mar Ivanios and his companions entered full communion with the Bishop of Rome, and the Syro-Malankara Church still prays daily for the unity of all Christ's disciples. The Gospel adds a word about how this peace spreads. “No one after lighting a lamp hides it under a jar, or puts it under a bed, but puts it on a lampstand, so that those who enter may see the light.” The light of Easter is not for hiding. Then Jesus says something sharp: “Then pay attention to how you listen; for to those who have, more will be given; and from those who do not have, even what they seem to have will be taken away.” The one who listens with faith receives more; the one who hears without receiving loses even the little he thought he had. St Augustine told his hearers that the sound of the preacher's words strikes the ear, but the true Teacher is within, and only he makes the word take root (in substance).

How do we live this Wednesday of Qyomtho? Look honestly for one wall in your life: a relative, a neighbor, a colleague, a Christian of another Church you have kept at a distance. Take one step toward them this week: a greeting, a phone call, a visit, a prayer said for them by name. Pray for the unity of Christians, especially among the Churches of the St Thomas tradition in Kerala. And watch how you listen: at the Holy Qurbono, try to hear the readings as if for the first time; at home, switch off the screen for ten minutes and let the Gospel speak; with others, listen to understand rather than to answer. The lamp is lit; let it stand on the lampstand of a peaceful life.
outline: Ask: is there a wall in my life that Christ has broken but I keep rebuilding?
Point 1 · Brought near by the blood of Christ
Far and near, Gentile and Jew, in the commonwealth of promise.
The dividing wall broken down in his flesh.
Point 3 · Pay attention to how you listen
The lamp on the lampstand and the listening heart.
live: Take one step across a wall (Ephesians 2:14)
Choose one person you have kept at a distance and greet, call, visit, or pray for them by name this week.
Before the readings at the Holy Qurbono, pray: “Lord, let me hear this as if for the first time.”
2027-04-07.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, you are our peace. In your flesh you made both groups into one and broke down the dividing wall of hostility; through you we all have access in one Spirit to the Father. Bring near all who are far off, heal the divisions in our families, our parishes and our Churches, and keep us from rebuilding the walls you have broken. Set the lamp of your Easter light on the lampstand of our lives, and teach us to listen to your word with faith, so that more may be given us. To you be glory with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: At the altar the risen Lord, who is our peace, gathers those who were far and those who were near into one Body, and in the Holy Qurbono he gives us the peace that no wall can keep out.

quick: In Christ, those who were far off have been brought near by his blood, into the hope of Israel's covenants.
He is our peace: he broke down the dividing wall of hostility, and through him all have access in one Spirit to the Father.
A lamp is put on a lampstand; pay attention to how you listen.
2027-04-07.action: Take one step this week toward someone you have kept at a distance.
2027-04-07.question: Which wall in my life am I still rebuilding?

family.explain: St Paul says that Jesus is our peace. Long ago there was a wall between groups of people who would not be friends. Jesus broke down that wall by dying on the cross and rising again, so that everyone can be one family in God. Sometimes we build walls too, when we stay angry or refuse to talk to someone. Jesus wants to help us break them down.
family.intention: We pray for families and neighbors who are not speaking to each other, that Jesus may bring them peace.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we need to make peace with this week?”

illus: Two brothers in a village near Pathanamthitta had not spoken for eleven years over a strip of land between their houses. Their aged mother lived with the elder brother and went to church alone. In the week after New Sunday the younger brother's daughter, home from nursing college, heard the reading “he has broken down the dividing wall.” That evening she walked across the strip of land with a box of Easter cake and knocked on her uncle's door. Her uncle opened it, looked at her for a long time, and called his wife. The brothers did not settle the land that year. But on the next Sunday they stood together in church for the first time in eleven years, with their mother between them.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you are our peace. Break down every wall among us and open our ears to your word. Amen.
share: But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ (Ephesians 2:13). When did I feel far from God, and how did he bring me near?
He is our peace; in his flesh he has made both groups into one and has broken down the dividing wall (Ephesians 2:14). Which wall in my life does Christ want to break down?
Pay attention to how you listen (Luke 8:18). How do I listen to God's word, and to others?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, you are our peace.
interc: For the unity of all Christians, especially among the Churches of the St Thomas tradition.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, and for friendship between Christians and Jews.
For families and neighbors divided by quarrels, that the risen Lord may bring them peace.
For communities wounded by caste and prejudice, that all may know they are one in Christ.
For ourselves, that we may listen to God's word with faith and let his light shine.
pm.close: Father, through your Son, who is our peace, you have brought near those who were far off and given all of us access to you in one Spirit. Break down the walls that divide us, make us people who listen with faith, and let the light of the Resurrection shine through our lives. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! On Easter evening the Lord said to his disciples, Peace be with you. Today St Paul tells us how deep that peace goes: he is our peace; in his flesh he has made both groups into one and has broken down the dividing wall, that is, the hostility between us (Ephesians 2:14).

We who were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ, brought into the hope of Israel's covenants. Through him all of us have access in one Spirit to the Father. Christ has already broken the wall. Our part is to stop rebuilding it in our families, our parishes, and between Churches.

In the Gospel Jesus says that no one hides a lamp under a jar. The light of Easter is not for hiding. And he adds: pay attention to how you listen (Luke 8:18). The one who listens with faith receives more.
So this week let us take one step across a wall: a greeting, a call, a visit, a prayer for someone by name. And let us listen to God's word as if for the first time. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! St Paul says that Jesus is our peace. When people are angry with each other, it is like building a wall between them. Jesus came to break down walls, so that we can all be friends in God's family. Is there someone you had a fight with? Today you can say sorry, or just say hello with a smile.

intro: On Wednesday after New Sunday: those far off brought near, the wall broken down in Christ's flesh, and the listening heart that lets the light shine.

points.h: Brought near by the blood of Christ
sub: The commonwealth of Israel and the covenants of promise.
q: Peace, peace, to the far and the near, says the LORD; and I will heal them.
There is no longer Jew or Greek, there is no longer slave or free, there is no longer male and female; for all of you are one in Christ Jesus.
points.apply: Thank God today for the gift of faith that brought you near, and pray for the Jewish people.

sub: The wall broken down in his flesh.
Hostility put to death on the Cross.
Access in one Spirit to the Father.
q: For a child has been born for us, a son given to us; authority rests upon his shoulders; and he is named Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives.
points.apply: Take one step this week toward someone you have kept at a distance.

points.h: Pay attention to how you listen
sub: To those who have, more will be given.
q: Speak, for your servant is listening.
But be doers of the word, and not merely hearers who deceive themselves.
points.apply: Before the readings at the Holy Qurbono, pray to hear them as if for the first time.

concl: The risen Christ is our peace: he has broken down every dividing wall and brought all into one Body.
His light is not for hiding, and those who listen with faith receive more.
2027-04-07.resolve: Stop rebuilding the walls Christ has broken: take one step toward reconciliation, pray for Christian unity, and listen to God's word with a ready heart.
